# Extend power-up catalogue with combat-coupled power-ups

## Summary
Add P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, and P7 Teleport entries to the power-up type catalogue (extending from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT). Each entry includes id, name, icon reference, duration/stack semantics, and a hook identifier for its effect function.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - P3 Shield entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P3`, name `Shield`, duration 15s, single-use (consumed on pop), effect hook `shieldAbsorb`.
- [ ] **AC2 - P4 Bomb entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P4`, name `Bomb`, duration `null` (not timed), single-use, effect hook `bombClear`, with a note that it does not damage enemies per GDD.
- [ ] **AC3 - P6 Phase Shift entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P6`, name `Phase Shift`, duration 3s, single-use (refreshable), effect hook `phaseShift`.
- [ ] **AC4 - P7 Teleport entry:** Catalogue entry with id `P7`, name `Teleport`, stack semantics FIFO (accumulates uses), effect hook `teleport`, with HUD count indicator.
- [ ] **AC5 - Ascending order:** Entries are listed in ascending GDD id order: P3, P4, P6, P7 - matching the round-robin spawn order.
- [ ] **AC6 - No behavioural code:** The catalogue entries are data-only (id, name, icon, duration, stack, hook); no effect implementation lives here.

## Deliverables
- Extended `src/powerups/types.ts` with P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries

## Key Files:
- `src/powerups/types.ts` - add 4 catalogue entries
data.title: Catalogue extension: P3, P4, P6, P7 entries

# Extend effects module with combat-coupled power-up behaviours

## Summary
Extend `src/powerups/effects.ts` (or create it if not yet present from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) with the four combat-coupled effect implementations. Each effect function receives the scene context and ship reference, manages its own state/timer, and exposes an API for the collision pass to query state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Shield effect (shieldAbsorb):** Returns an effect object with `isActive`, `pop()` method, `apply()` that renders a bubble around the ship, `onHit()` that absorbs one hit and pops, and a timer that expires after 15s. `recollect()` refreshes timer to 15s.
- [ ] **AC2 - Bomb effect (bombClear):** Returns an effect with `apply()` that removes all on-screen enemy bullets (iterates the bullet collection and destroys each), does NOT damage enemy entities. Shows a brief HUD notice string. `recollect()` is a benign no-op.
- [ ] **AC3 - Phase Shift effect (phaseShift):** Returns an effect with `isActive`, `isInvulnerable` flag set to true during active period, `apply()` that renders a ghost outline of the ship, 3s duration timer, `recollect()` refreshes to 3s.
- [ ] **AC4 - Teleport effect (teleport):** Returns an effect with a FIFO stack of remaining uses, `consume()` removes one use and returns true if any remain, `getCount()` returns remaining uses. `apply()` triggers safe-spot resolution (see AC5). On teleport success, grants P6 Phase Shift (3s).
- [ ] **AC5 - Safe-spot resolution (resolveSafeSpot):** A pure function that takes current ship position, travel direction, enemy positions, bullet positions, and safe radius. Returns the nearest safe position along the travel ray (no enemy/bullet within safe radius), clamped to screen bounds. If no safe spot in travel direction, returns nearest on-screen safe position (GDD fallback).
- [ ] **AC6 - Effect factory:** A `createEffect(type, scene, ship)` factory function that dispatches to the correct implementation based on the power-up id.

## Deliverables
- Extended `src/powerups/effects.ts` with shield, bomb, phase shift, teleport, safe-spot, and factory

## Key Files:
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` - add all 4 effect implementations + safe-spot + factory
- `src/core/constants.ts` - reads teleportSafeRadius and flashResetDuration from constants
data.title: Effects module: shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift, teleport

# GymPowerUpsCombat scene - combat-coupled power-up gym

## Summary
Create `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` - a standalone gym scene that demonstrates P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, and P7 Teleport against E1 Scout enemies with shooting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Scene registration:** Scene key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`, registered in the scene loader, auto-discovered by the gym index, listed alongside other gym scenes.
- [ ] **AC2 - Player ship:** Reuses `src/entities/Player.ts` with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap. No auto-fire (weapon power-ups are out of scope).
- [ ] **AC3 - Scout formation:** V-formation of ~6 E1 Scouts (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts`), with a SHOOT toggle button that enables aimed fire at the ship live position (parameterising the aim target from the fixed demo target).
- [ ] **AC4 - Round-robin spawner:** Spawns P3 to P4 to P6 to P7 in ascending GDD order, one every 5 seconds, each remaining stationary for a 5-second lifetime. Grow from scale 0 to full in 0.5s, shrink to nothing in 0.5s (delta-time driven, matching non-combat gym constants).
- [ ] **AC5 - 3% collection gate:** Drops are only collectible when their current scale > 3% of full size; collection via overlap with ship; uncollected drops fade with no effect.
- [ ] **AC6 - Effect application:** On collection, the corresponding effect from `src/powerups/effects.ts` is applied: P3 to shield bubble, P4 to bullet clear, P6 to phase shift, P7 to teleport (FIFO). Effects render their visuals and manage their own timers.
- [ ] **AC7 - Hit response (AC8):** Collision with an enemy body or enemy bullet, when no P3 shield or P6 phase shift is active, triggers a flash + brief invulnerability + reposition (no lives, no game over). Values from `src/core/constants.ts`.
- [ ] **AC8 - Hit-check suppression:** During P3 active (absorbing) or P6 active (phase shift), hit checks are suppressed - no flash/reset occurs. P3 consumes one absorption on first hit and pops.
- [ ] **AC9 - HUD reuse:** Attaches the standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7). No lives counter in this scene.
- [ ] **AC10 - Back button:** Shared `<- INDEX` back button present, navigates to the gym index scene.

## Deliverables
- New `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` scene file
- Parameterised Scout fire target (ship position) - minimal change to `src/entities/Scout.ts` if needed
- HUD attachment in the scene (reusing `src/ui/HUD.ts` unchanged)

## Key Files:
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` - new combat gym scene
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` - parameterise aim target if needed (small change)
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` - reuse unchanged (import only)

Test the P7 Teleport effect implementation and safe-spot resolution logic in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - FIFO stack semantics:** Each collection pushes to a stack; `consume()` pops the earliest entry and returns true if any remain.

# Fix tree_coverage helper reading children from wrong JSON key

## Summary
The shared plan-skill helper _wl_show_children (skills/shared/tree_coverage.py) reads data['workItem']['children'], but `wl show <id> --children --json` returns the children list at the TOP level (data['children']), alongside 'workItem'. As a result run_coverage_review sees zero children and reports vacuous 100% coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. _wl_show_children returns the top-level 'children' list from wl show --children --json.
2. run_coverage_review reports real child AC coverage (child_summary populated).
3. Existing tests for tree_coverage pass (updated if they encoded the wrong shape).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a work item with children.
2. Run python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared'); import tree_coverage as tc; print(tc._wl_show_children('<id>'))" — returns [] even though wl show --children --json returns the children.

## Notes
- discovered-from:AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC (plan run exposed the bug; workaround applied via monkeypatch).
- File: /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tree_coverage.py (~line 145).
- Agent infrastructure (.pi/agent/skills) — do not edit without explicit authorisation.
data.title: Fix tree_coverage helper reading children from wrong JSON key

# GymSwarm AC3 (swarm aimed fire hits player) is flaky under full-suite parallel load — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

`GymSwarm.test.ts > AC3 — a player bullet destroys a swarm member; a swarm shot hitting the player respawns it` failed once during the implement finish-gate full-suite run for AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ (14 tests | 1 failed, 156 ms — not a timeout) while all ad-hoc full-suite runs (4× 526/526) passed. The transient burst/hit state is missed under parallel CPU load when the test relies on a single interval-boundary clock jump and a single volley's random spread.

## Users

- **CI / developer** — wants `npm --silent test` to be deterministic under full-suite parallel load, so a passing gate means the same on retry — not a one-off flake that erodes trust in gym coverage.
  - *Story:* As a developer running the gate, I run the full suite once and the verdict is stable, so I don't chase false failures.
- **Gym playtester / gym maintainer** — wants AC3 to faithfully prove swarm aimed fire can hit and respawn the player, not merely that one lucky volley happened to land.
  - *Story:* As a playtester, I trust AC3 as a specification: swarm bursts are aimed at the live player and a hit causes destruction + respawn + invulnerability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — AC3 deterministic under parallel load:** `GymSwarm.test.ts > AC3` does not depend on a single `scene.time.now += SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL + 500` boundary jump; it polls with bounded quarter-interval clock steps so the swarm re-fires fresh aimed volleys until one lands (mirrors the GymScout AC2 fix in commit `e48b046`), and passes reliably under `npm --silent test` (full-suite parallel). *At current HEAD the per-enemy GymSwarm scene is retired into `GymEnemies` (enemyKey=swarm) — see Key Files — so this AC is satisfied by the landed poll fix at `38fddc6` and its preserved semantics in `Swarm` + `GymFormationScene`.*
- **AC2 — Hit semantics preserved:** After the player bullet destroys one swarm member (`aliveCount` decrements, victim `bodyVisible` false, bullet consumed), a subsequent swarm burst that reaches the player increments `getPlayerHitCount()`, respawns the player at `PLAYER_SPAWN`, sets `isPlayerInvulnerable() === true`, and `playDestructionSound` is called.
- **AC3 — No single-volley luck dependency:** The hit poll is bounded (e.g. ≤160 quarter-interval steps) but never asserts on the first volley's random spread (`±0.15 rad` per bullet); comments measure/document the ~12% all-miss rate at full-suite load that the poll guards against.
- **AC4 — Validation/tests:** `npm --silent test` passes and remains stable across repeated full-suite runs (at least 3 consecutive greens at the fix commit); no production behaviour changed — only test determinism.
- **AC5 — Documentation:** Code comments explain the spread-vs-poll rationale and the mirror to `e48b046`; no README/wiki change required beyond those comments (production behaviour unchanged).

## Constraints

- Small, chore-scope test-hardening only: no production logic change (Swarm firing cadence and aim remain unchanged); no new behaviour or scene refactor.
- Keep the bound tight: poll loop must terminate deterministically (bounded steps, no wall-clock `setTimeout` wait).
- Follows the established gym flake pattern (`c2aaa54` GymDiver AC1, `e48b046` GymScout AC2, `38fddc6` GymSwarm AC3/GymTank AC3) — deterministic `tick(dt)` + frozen `scene.time.now` advancement.
- Do not block on Enemy Design tooling (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN); this is a standalone stability fix.

## Existing state

- At HEAD the fix for this exact flake has already landed as part of `AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM` (`38fddc6`, on `dev` and ancestor of `HEAD`): `GymSwarm.test.ts` AC3 no longer does a single `+ SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL + 500` jump; it captures `hitsBefore = getPlayerHitCount()` and loops `for (…; i<160 && hitCount===hitsBefore; i++) { scene.time.now += SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL/4; scene.tick(0.05); }` so fresh aimed volleys re-fire until one lands — exactly the GymScout AC2 poll idiom (`e48b046`). The pre-fix single-volley window missed hits at ~12% of volleys at full-suite load.
- Parent epic AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC (`Player cannot be moved in enemy/power-up gyms`) is `done` at `38fddc6` with suite green (31 files, 543 tests), and its flake siblings `GymDiver AC1` (`c2aaa54`) and `GymScout AC2` (`e48b046`) are on `dev`.
- GymTank AC3's companion wall-clock flake was fixed the same commit by driving drift via accumulated `tick(dt)` instead of `setTimeout`.
- Per-enemy gym scenes (`GymSwarm`, `GymScout`, `GymTank`, `GymDiver`, etc.) were retired at `5bbaa2d` into the single config-driven `GymEnemies` scene (enemyKey=swarm/scout/tank/…) backed by `GymFormationScene`. At current HEAD (`495b26b`) the AC3 semantics are covered by `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` (burst/aim) + `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` (hit→respawn+invulnerability). Production burst constants remain in `src/entities/Swarm.ts` (`SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL = 900`, `SWARM_BULLET_SPEED = 180`).

## Desired change

- Harden `GymSwarm.test.ts` AC3 to the deterministic poll form described in AC1 (if not already at HEAD, apply it; if already at HEAD, verify and formalise as the acceptance contract) so the test never depends on one random-spread volley.
- Keep the bounded hit window (or lengthen only if needed for stability) and add/retain comments explaining the spread-vs-poll rationale and the mirror to `e48b046`.
- Verify with repeated full-suite runs (`≥3` consecutive `npm --silent test` greens) and leave a comment linking the prior failure, the fix commits, and the verification.
- *Note at current HEAD:* the desired poll is already on `dev` history (`38fddc6`) and the file is retired; the contract is preserved by retaining the Swarm + GymFormationScene coverage — no new file edits required unless a regression is found during verification.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — burst constants `SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL`, `SWARM_BULLET_SPEED` and `tryFireBurstBullet` spread contract (±0.15 rad)
- `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` — Swarm entity unit tests (burst interval, aimed fire, destruction, formation)
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — shared formation base: burst collection, hit/respawn + invulnerability, deterministic `tick(dt)` + live aim seam
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — core scene AC3 coverage (enemy bullet hits player → `getPlayerHitCount`/respawn/`isPlayerInvulnerable` + blink)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — config-driven swarm gym (enemyKey=swarm) wiring Swarm into GymFormationScene (retired GymSwarm.ts at `5bbaa2d`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — GymEnemies smoke/config tests (retired GymSwarm.test.ts heritage)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts` (historical, retired at `5bbaa2d`) — reference poll idiom (`e48b046`: `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` + quarter-cue steps) — see git history
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.test.ts` (historical, retired at `5bbaa2d`) — companion deterministic drift fix (`38fddc6`) — reference only

## Related work

- **AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC** — `Player cannot be moved in enemy and power-up gym scenes` (parent epic, `done` at `38fddc6`; scheme-aware gym work that first surfaced this one-off)
- **AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ** — `Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes` (finish-gate run where this AC3 first failed once)
- **AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C** — `GymScout.test.ts is flaky under full-suite parallel load` (sibling flake epic; describes GymSwarm AC3/GymTank AC3/GymDiver AC1 fixes and their expected verifications; `done` at `38fddc6`)
- **AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM** — `fix flaky timer-sensitive gym tests` (`38fddc6`: landed the GymSwarm AC3 poll + GymTank drift fixes; verified 3× full-suite green)
- **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** — `GymDiver AC1 (diver x locked during dive) is wall-clock flaky` (deterministic `tick` pattern `c2aaa54`, mirrored here)
- Commit `e48b046` — `GymScout AC2` quarter-cue poll idiom (pattern mirrored for Swarm)
- Commit `c2aaa54` — `GymDiver AC1` deterministic rewrite (pattern mirrored for Tank/Swarm)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: fix already landed but brief stale.** Mitigation: intake formalises the *contract* (poll, not single jump) so future edits cannot regress it; at current HEAD the contract is preserved via `Swarm` + `GymFormationScene` after the `5bbaa2d` retirement — verify via those tests.
- **Risk: hidden timing coupling (Phaser `time.now` vs real loop).** Mitigation: keep frozen-clock advancement (`scene.time.now += …`) + `tick(0.05)` only — no `setTimeout` waits.
- **Risk: over-lengthening the window masks a real aim bug.** Mitigation: AC2 keeps directional assertions (mean burst aims at `PLAYER_SPAWN`); poll bounds remain tight (≤160 steps).
- **Risk: scope creep into Swarm production tuning.** Mitigation: explicitly out of scope — only the test hardens.
- **Assumption:** Intake may proceed without operator Q&A — the failure mode, proposed fix, and reference commits are explicit in the item; reasonable assumptions documented here.
- **Assumption:** Operator permits proceeding without further questions (prompt allows recording open questions and marking `needs-producer-review` only if blocked — not blocked here).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- No interview round was run — the seed item already contains the failure observation (`156 ms`, not a timeout; `4× 526/526` ad-hoc greens), the root-cause hypothesis (single boundary jump + single random-spread volley + bounded 8 s hit window; ~12% all-miss at load), and the proposed fix topology (poll for burst, as in `e48b046`, and/or lengthen window). Research inspected: `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.test.ts` at HEAD, `src/entities/Swarm.ts` constants, commits `e48b046`/`c2aaa54`/`38fddc6`, and related items AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C / AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC / AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ / AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW. If the producer prefers a different stability threshold (e.g. more/fewer full-suite repetitions or a different bound) that can be adjusted at plan/implement with no brief change.
data.title: GymSwarm AC3 (swarm aimed fire hits player) is flaky under full-suite parallel load

# Test: Wipe detection, countdown, and respawn in GymFormationScene

## Summary

Write automated tests in GymFormationScene.test.ts covering the new wipe detection, countdown, and respawn behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 - Wipe detection test:** When all enemies are destroyed (aliveCount transitions to 0), the scene enters the respawn countdown state within one tick. Assert isRespawnCountdownActive() returns true.
- [ ] **AC2 - Countdown progression:** Over 3 seconds of tick(dt), the countdown progresses from 3 to 2 to 1. Assert getRespawnCountdownRemaining() reflects the correct remaining time.
- [ ] **AC3 - Respawn after countdown:** After the countdown reaches 0, all enemies are recreated at their original formation positions. Assert aliveCount returns to config.count. Verify entities are at correct startX/startY-derived positions.
- [ ] **AC4 - Bullet cleanup on respawn:** After countdown expires and before respawn, all enemy bullets are cleared. Assert activeBullets returns empty array after respawn.
- [ ] **AC5 - shootEnabled preserved:** If shooting was enabled before wipe, it remains enabled after respawn. Assert shootingEnabled returns true after respawn if it was true before.
- [ ] **AC6 - Countdown restart on scene tear-down:** If the scene is destroyed while countdown is active, no errors occur on restart. Assert no crash or stale state.
- [ ] **AC7 - Existing tests still pass:** All existing GymFormationScene tests continue to pass.

## Implementation Notes

- Tests should use the same mocking approach as existing tests in GymFormationScene.test.ts.
- Use the public getters isRespawnCountdownActive() and getRespawnCountdownRemaining() to observe countdown state.
- Verify formation positions after respawn by checking entity x/y against config.startX + offset.col * config.spacingX, config.startY + offset.row * config.spacingY.
- Use the existing test helpers and Phaser test scene patterns.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts - Add wipe detection, countdown, and respawn tests.

## Dependencies

- AH-0MTHCD0BQ000JFZ4 (implement) - Must be completed first.

# Upgrade getEngineSoundLevel to continuous thrust-scaled output

## Summary
Upgrade `getEngineSoundLevel` from a binary placeholder (0 or 1) to a continuous level in [0, 1] scaled by `thrustAcceleration`, mirroring the flame growth model.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1** — `FourDirectionalModel.getEngineSoundLevel` returns `0` when no thrust keys are held; returns `min(1, thrustAcceleration / FLAME_REF_THRUST)` when any thrust key is held.
- **AC2** — `AsteroidsModel.getEngineSoundLevel` returns `0` when no thrust keys are held; returns `min(1, thrustAcceleration / FLAME_REF_THRUST)` when forward/turnLeft/turnRight is held.
- **AC3** — At `thrustAcceleration = 0`, the level is always `0` regardless of key state (consistent with `flameGrowthRate` returning 0).
- **AC4** — `getEngineActivity` remains unchanged (key-specific engine selection unaffected).
- **AC5** — `MovementModel.tick` and all physics remain unchanged.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite passes with no regressions.

## Deliverables
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — upgraded `getEngineSoundLevel` for both models

## Key Files
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — FourDirectionalModel and AsteroidsModel implementations
- `src/utils/flame.ts` — `FLAME_REF_THRUST = 300` constant (reuse analogously)
- `src/core/config.ts` — `DEFAULT_CONFIG.thrustAcceleration`

## Dependencies
- Depends on test work item `AH-0MTHEDYG6009UM3K` (tests written first, TDD)

## Implementation Notes
- Use the same scaling ratio as the flame model: `level = min(1, thrustAcceleration / FLAME_REF_THRUST)`
- This keeps audio and VFX in sync — same scaling basis, proportional behavior

# Implement thruster hum in effects.ts

## Summary
Add a sustained thruster hum to `src/audio/effects.ts` using Web Audio synthesis — a single oscillator+gain pair that can be driven per-frame, with gain envelope for fade-in/decay (no clicks/pops).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1** — The thruster hum uses procedural Web Audio only (no external assets): e.g., low sawtooth/square + sine undertone, filtered hum.
- **AC2** — Gain scales with thrust level: 0 when not thrusting, rises to max when thrusting, proportional to level parameter (from movement model).
- **AC3** — Volume ceiling ≤ 0.2 (consistent with existing player cues per GDD §7.3).
- **AC4** — Fade-in: gain ramps from 0 to target over ≤ 100 ms at reference thrust (faster at higher thrust).
- **AC5** — Fade-out: gain decays to 0 at ~4× the growth rate, with no clicks/pops (exponential envelope).
- **AC6** — Retriggering thrust while decaying restarts the ramp from current gain.
- **AC7** — Single oscillator+gain pair: holding thrust does not stack oscillators; releasing and re-pressing does not leak AudioNodes.
- **AC8** — Safe no-op without AudioContext (headless tests, autoplay-blocked browsers).
- **AC9** — The hum is distinct from all existing blip/cue sounds (different wave type/frequency range).
- **AC10** — Full project test suite passes with no regressions.

## Deliverables
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new thruster hum interface + implementation

## Key Files
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — primary implementation file
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — dependent test item (written first)
- `src/utils/flame.ts` — reuse growth/decay timing constants analogously

## Dependencies
- Depends on test work item `AH-0MTHEDYG6009UM3K` tests being written first (TDD)

## Implementation Notes
- Pattern: single oscillator (low freq sawtooth/square) → gain node → destination
- API: `updateThrusterSound(level: number)` — called per-frame by Player/scene
- Gain envelope: exponential ramps for smooth transitions (avoid clicks)
- Frequency: low enough to be a "hum" (e.g., 60-120 Hz), with possible pitch modulation by thrust level
- Max volume: 0.15-0.2 (consistent with player cue ceiling)
data.title: Implement thruster hum in effects.ts

# Wire thruster audio in Player.ts

## Summary
Integrate the thruster hum audio into `Player.preUpdate` so the hum follows the active movement model each frame — starting/stopping with thrust input, using `getEngineSoundLevel` for the current thrust level.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1** — The thruster hum starts when any thrust key is held and stops when no thrust keys are held.
- **AC2** — The hum level is derived from `getEngineSoundLevel` + config, driving the audio per frame.
- **AC3** — In FourDirectional scheme: any arrow/WASD thrust key produces the hum.
- **AC4** — In Asteroids scheme: W/Up (forward) and A/Left, D/Right (turn) produce the hum.
- **AC5** — The hum stops when the ship is destroyed or the scene switches.
- **AC6** — No physics changes: `MovementModel.tick` and flame animation remain behaviorally unchanged.
- **AC7** — Full project test suite passes with no regressions.

## Deliverables
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — per-frame thruster audio integration in `preUpdate`

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `preUpdate` method, flame animation integration point
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — thruster hum API to call
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — `getEngineSoundLevel` for level derivation

## Dependencies
- Depends on `AH-0MTHEDYG6009UM3K` (getEngineSoundLevel upgraded)
- Depends on thruster hum implementation in effects.ts (item created after test)

## Implementation Notes
- In `Player.preUpdate`, call the thruster audio interface with the level from `getEngineSoundLevel`

- Ensure the hum is initialized on first thrust press and cleaned up on scene change
